title: Parsing an entry followed by an in-range entry
statement: Fix $w \geq 1$, and consider parsing an aux list whose first two entries are $(\mathrm{idx}, \mathrm{dir})$ and $(\mathrm{idx}', \mathrm{dir}')$, both with in-range indices $\mathrm{idx} < w$ and $\mathrm{idx}' < w$, followed by any further list $\mathrm{rest}$. Then parsing $(\mathrm{idx}, \mathrm{dir}) :: (\mathrm{idx}', \mathrm{dir}') :: \mathrm{rest}$ yields the triple $(\mathrm{idx}, \mathrm{dir}, \mathrm{false})$ — with no termination marker recorded — prepended to the parse of $(\mathrm{idx}', \mathrm{dir}') :: \mathrm{rest}$.
replaced:
Equational lemma: if an entry $(idx, dir)$ is immediately followed by another
in-range entry $(idx', dir')$, then $\mathrm{parseAux}$ emits the triple
$(\langle idx, h\rangle, dir, \mathrm{false})$ followed by the parse of the
remaining list starting at $(idx', dir')$.
